Whats that fancy web server/reverse proxy/load balance thing?
column3: a high-performance; open-source web server; reverse proxy; load balancer; and HTTP cache; designed for low memory usage and high concurrency.

column1: NSG meaning?
column3: a security feature in Azure that allows you to control inbound and outbound traffic to your Azure resources; it contains security rules that allow or deny traffic based on source and destination IP addresses; ports; and protocols.

column1: Two types of 'domains' that availability sets are grouped by ?/?
column3: The update process is given a 30-minute time to recover before maintenance on the next Update domain starts; The fault domain groups your VMs by common power source and network switch (x3 is default)

column1: Provides a dedicated private connectivity to Azure that doesn't travel over the internet?
column3: a service that provides a private connection between your on-premises infrastructure and Azure datacenters; it offers higher security; reliability; and speed compared to typical internet connections.

column1: Ways of running a small program or script: older/newer?
column3: WebJobs can be run through Azure App service on a more fixed cost basis; Azure Functions stand alone and only bill for the time your code is running

column1: BPG Meaning?
column3: Commonly used in the Internet to exchange routing and reachability information between two or more networks.

column1: This allows two Azure virtual networks to connect directly to each other; so they appear as one
column3: Networks can be in separate regions; Traffic is private and travels on MS backbone

column1: Command to switch from bash/PowerShell to pure Azure in a fancier CLI?
column3: You can type az commands directly here.

column1: LRS = ?? Redundant Storage / # of nines uptime rating?
column3: Locally Redundant Storage (LRS) replicates your data three times (x3) within a single data center in the same region; it provides 99.999999999% (11 nines) durability of objects over a given year.

column1: GRS = ?? Redundant Storage / # of nines uptime rating?
column3: Geo-Redundant Storage (GRS) replicates your data to a secondary region hundreds of miles away from the primary region; it provides 99.99999999999999% (16 nines) durability of objects over a given year.

column1: ZRS = ?? Redundant Storage / # of nines uptime rating?
column3: Zone-Redundant Storage (ZRS) replicates your data synchronously across three Azure availability zones in the same region; it provides 99.9999999999% (12 nines) durability of objects over a given year.

column1: Type of storage account if you need support for network file system (NFS)
column3: Recommended for enterprise or high-performance scale applications. Use this account type if you want a storage account that supports both Server Message Block (SMB) and NFS file shares.

column1: Premium Block Blobs & Premium File Share storage accounts support which redundancy options?
column3: Premium storage account type for block blobs and append blobs. Recommended for scenarios with high transaction rates or that use smaller objects or require consistently low storage latency.

column1: Type of storage account that only supports LRS redundancy?
column3: Only supports LRS redundancy because it is designed for high-performance workloads that require low latency and high IOPS; it is not intended for scenarios that require geo-redundancy or zone-redundancy.

column1: Storage account names must be between ?/? characters long?
column3: Storage account names must be between 3 and 24 characters in length; they can contain only lowercase letters and numbers; and must be unique across Azure.

column1: Azure Blob Storage Cool/Cold/Archive tiers: at least ?/?/? days?
column3: All four tiers can be set at the blob level; during or after upload. Only Hot/Cool/Cold can be set at the account level

column1: Data in the cool and cold access tiers can tolerate slightly lower?
column3: But cool/cold data still requires high durability; retrieval latency; and throughput characteristics similar to hot data. (doesn't have to be up all the time but when you need it you want it now)

column1: SMB Azure file shares can be cached on Windows Servers using?
column3: a service that allows you to centralize your file shares in Azure Files while keeping the flexibility; performance; and compatibility of an on-premises file server.

column1: Each individual Azure Queue message can be up to ? in size?
column3: Azure Queue Storage is a service for storing large numbers of messages that can be accessed from anywhere in the world via authenticated calls using HTTP or HTTPS

column1: Acronym for defense in depth layers?
column3: Physical Security / Identity & Access / Perimeter / Network / Compute Application / Data

column1: CSPM Meaning?
column3: a category of security tools that help organizations identify and remediate risks in their cloud environments; it provides continuous monitoring; assessment; and compliance management for cloud resources and configurations.

column1: Perform anomaly detection on your Azure activity logs using the native integration with?
column3: Defender for Cloud Apps (formerly Microsoft Cloud App Security) is a cloud access security broker (CASB) that provides visibility; control; and threat protection for cloud applications.

column1: Defender for Cloud helps you detect threats across: ?/?/?
column3: Azure services including Azure App Service; Azure SQL; Azure Storage Account; and more data services. Automatically classify your data in Azure SQL & get vulnerability assessments of SQL and Storage; also network defenses.

column1: Defender for Cloud; 3 things it do for security?
column3: Continuously assess – Know your security posture. Identify and track vulnerabilities. Secure – Harden resources and services with Azure Security Benchmark. Defend – Detect and resolve threats to resources; workloads; and services.

column1: provides a set of guidelines for security and compliance best practices based on common compliance frameworks
column3: Recommendations help you reduce the attack surface across each of your resources are supported by Azure Security Benchmark

column1: Bandwidth refers to data moving in and out of Azure datacenters. Which can sometimes be free?
column3: For outbound data transfers (data leaving Azure datacenters); data transfer pricing is based on zones; A zone is a geographical grouping of Azure regions for billing purposes.

column1: Acronym for the 5 sections of Azure Advisor?
column3: Security; Performance; Reliability; Operational Excellence; Cost

column1: Acronym for the 3 levels of Service Health view?
column3: Azure Status; Service Health; Resource Health

column1: Tool where you write and run queries against the data Azure Monitor collects
column3: Azure Log Analytics; it uses a powerful query language called Kusto Query Language (KQL) to analyze and visualize your monitoring data.

column1: Three things you are always responsible for when using a cloud provider?
column3: info and data stores; devices allowed to connect; accounts and identities of people/services/devices in your org.

column1: Three things the cloud provider is always responsible for?
column3: physical security; network infrastructure; host hardware and virtualization layer.

column1: Adding more CPU's or RAM to a virtual machine is an example of:
column3: vertical scaling (or scaling up) means increasing or decreasing the capabilities of resources

column1: Adding additional virtual machines or containers is an example of:
column3: horizontal scaling (or scaling out) means adding (or subtracting) more instances of resources

column1: Two types of predictability in MS Azure Well-Architechted Framework ?/?
column3: Performance predictability ensures that your applications consistently meet performance requirements under varying loads; Cost predictability helps you manage and forecast your cloud expenses effectively.

column1: Term for feature that can deploy additional resources to meet the demand
column3: Autoscaling automatically adjusts the number of active servers or resources based on current demand; ensuring optimal performance and cost-efficiency.

column1: Feature/tools often available in cloud environments to help better plan resource deployments
column3: Data analytics tools can analyze historical usage patterns and predict future resource needs; helping organizations optimize their cloud deployments.

column1: What item in shared responsibility has a hard line down the middle and is never iffy?
column3: On-Prem and IaaS = YOU / PaaS and SaaS = Cloud Provider

column1: Azure has a cloud based solution for this virtualization platform
column3: Azure VMware Solution (AVS) is a service that allows you to run your VMware workloads natively on Azure; it provides a seamless migration path for VMware-based applications and workloads to the cloud.

column1: Term focusing on the speed and ease of allocating and deallocating resources
column3: Agility refers to the speed and ease while Elasticity is more about the automatic scaling of resources based on demand.
